evidence.note: Started the server as a background process, checked /_health via curl, and set up a boto3 smoke test for create-bucket/put/get/list/delete — real boto3 round-trips against core operations, not just assuming correctness.
When the server crashed on startup, caught it via log inspection, installed missing deps, restarted and re-ran health + admin + boto3 checks — a genuine run-observe-fix verification loop.

Ran progressively broader boto3 smoke tests covering versioning, tagging, multipart, presigned GET, CopyObject directives, and multi-object delete with versionId — happy-path verification across many advanced features, beyond mere core ops.

Edge/negative behaviors (namespace XML parsing, quota overwrite deltas, versioned emptiness, error codes) were addressed by reasoning/patching ('likely grader failures') rather than by explicit error-code assertions or edge-case tests.

Submitted as complete with NO concurrency/load test, NO explicit error-code negative assertions, and NO console DOM/testid interaction test — the console was never exercised at all, and header-vs-query signing edge cases were not systematically checked.

reasoning: The agent clearly runs the real boto3 client against core operations plus versioning/multipart/tagging/presigned/copy/multi-delete happy paths and gates a run-fix loop on live server output, exceeding the level-5 anchor (core ops + health round-trip). But it stops well short of level 8: no concurrency/load test, no explicit error-code or edge-behavior assertions (ranged/416, EntityTooSmall, conditional GET/PUT, cross-tenant codes were patched-by-reasoning, not verified), and crucially no console DOM/testid verification despite the console being half the score. This broad-but-happy-path boto3 verification with major gaps places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
